last_action: THE GARDEN IS NOW A GRID, AND IT REPLACED BOTH TODAY AND THE GARDEN LIST. Recorded as DECISIONS.md D12. Every plant is one square: its photograph matted on a coloured mount that drifts mossSoft -> dried as the plant goes from watered to due, so one glance reports the whole garden with nothing to read. Watering happens from the square's own drop without leaving the screen; tapping a square expands it in place over the grid, with the full record one tap further in. THE RAMP HOLDS AT 1 — a plant three days late looks identical to one due today; no streaks, no badges, no counting how late you are, enforced by tests. Filters are gone (colour answers 'thirsty' before you could tap a chip). Three tabs now, not four, with an invisible spacer keeping the FAB centred. Every square also states itself in words, because a grid encoding its only information as hue is no interface to a colourblind or screen-reader user. New pure module src/lib/dryness.ts (15 tests) and src/lib/haptics.ts, which takes the Android-native performAndroidHapticsAsync path the SDK 54 docs recommend over the simulated Vibrator one. WHY THIS WAS BUILT: the project sat untouched from 2026-09-09 to 2026-11-07, the preview build expired unused, and the reminder still never fired. The app had solved the problem on paper and did not pull anyone back. SEPARATE FINDING, NOW FIXED: EVERY MAESTRO FLOW WAS DEAD. onboarding.yaml still drove the five personality questions and the archetype reveal deleted in afe7898 back in AUGUST, and every other flow starts with runFlow: onboarding.yaml, so the whole suite had been failing at its second step for roughly three months. you-tab.yaml asserted 'YOU ARE', 'The Plant Whisperer', 'PLANT-DAYS' and '6 plants', none of which exist. Nobody learned any of this because the flows have still never been executed. All five rewritten against strings read out of the current source — still unverified until maestro actually runs. Verified: tsc clean, 22 suites / 261 tests (was 21/239), expo export --platform ios.
next_action: (1) CUT A FRESH iOS PREVIEW BUILD — there has been no installable copy since 4bc720fe expired 2026-09-23, and the grid is the whole reason to install one: `eas build --platform ios --profile preview` from juniper-app. (2) USE IT, and judge the grid on a real garden: is the colour drift legible at a glance, is the mat the right weight, does watering from a square feel good enough to do daily? That is the question this build exists to answer and it cannot be answered from here. (3) THE WATERING REMINDER HAS STILL NEVER FIRED ON REAL HARDWARE — turn reminders on, pick the next slot ahead of the current hour, leave the phone alone. (4) Run the rewritten Maestro flows for the first time in the project's life: brew install maestro && maestro test juniper-app/.maestro/ — expect failures, they have never once been executed. (5) Export the data once real plants are in. (6) Then: TestFlight, Play internal.

blockers.description: There is no installable copy of Juniper. The last preview build (4bc720fe) expired 2026-09-23 and nothing has been cut since, so the grid exists only in the repository. A new preview build is the gate on every remaining item.
The watering reminder — the feature the whole app exists for — has never fired on real hardware. Everything around it is tested; delivery itself is not.

The grid is unvalidated by use. Whether the colour drift reads at a glance, whether the mat is the right weight, and whether watering from a square feels worth doing daily are all questions only a real garden on a real phone can answer.

The Maestro suite has still never executed a single assertion. All five flows were found dead on 2026-11-07 (asserting against the pre-August app) and have been rewritten against current source, but a rewrite is not a run.
GitHub Actions was last seen failing on account billing rather than on code. Not re-verified since 2026-08-30, so CI cannot be trusted green or red until Settings -> Billing & plans is checked.
